name: Ionic
summary: A cross-platform UI toolkit that publishes web components for mobile-oriented interfaces, adds framework adapters and navigation primitives, and detects browser or native platform capabilities at runtime.

features.name: Web component UI primitives
features.description: The fixed core package defines Ionic elements such as ion-toolbar through Stencil component metadata and exports shared lifecycle, gesture, animation, configuration, and overlay utilities. The component package is therefore a browser custom-element surface rather than a framework-specific widget tree.
benefits: Keeps the primary component contract usable from plain web applications
Makes component lifecycle and DOM integration explicit
costs: DOM lifecycle and browser capabilities constrain portability
Component state crosses the custom-element and application-framework boundaries

features.name: Framework adapter packages
features.description: The repository contains separate Angular, React, Vue, and corresponding router packages that wrap or integrate the core Ionic components with framework conventions. These packages are distinct published surfaces, so framework integration is layered over the shared web-component core.
benefits: Allows framework applications to retain framework-native composition patterns
Keeps the core component implementation reusable across adapters
costs: Adapter behavior and release compatibility must track the core package
Multiple framework packages multiply integration and testing paths

features.name: Navigation and overlay lifecycle
features.description: The fixed source includes ion-nav stack operations and controller-managed overlays such as modal, alert, popover, loading, and toast. These APIs maintain application-visible lifecycle transitions around page views and transient UI elements.
benefits: Provides reusable page-stack and transient-overlay state transitions
Centralizes presentation and dismissal behavior across adapters
costs: Stack and overlay transitions introduce ordering and cleanup obligations
Application routing policy remains distinct from component lifecycle management

features.name: Platform and native capability boundary
features.description: Ionic detects browser, mobile, PWA, Electron, Cordova, and Capacitor conditions through configurable platform predicates, while native utilities expose capability-dependent behavior. The fixed source keeps platform detection and native integration behind shared web APIs.
benefits: Lets UI behavior adapt to browser and host capabilities
Provides one application-facing platform predicate surface
costs: User-agent, media-query, and host globals can misrepresent capabilities
Native bridge availability and platform-specific behavior remain conditional

mathematical_views.question: How do component registration, DOM lifecycle callbacks, shared utilities, and framework adapter edges determine a UI element's observable state?
assumptions: Custom elements are modeled as nodes with lifecycle transitions
Adapter packages are integration edges to the same core component nodes
Browser rendering and framework scheduler internals are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which page-stack and overlay transitions are reachable through Ionic navigation and controller APIs?
assumptions: Pages and overlays are stateful resources with push, present, dismiss, and lifecycle transitions
The view abstracts animation timing and framework router internals
An API transition is not evidence that all application routes are mutually compatible

mathematical_views.question: How does Ionic classify the current host and select platform-sensitive behavior?
assumptions: Platform predicates observe host/browser signals and optional custom methods
Cordova and Capacitor are modeled as optional native capability edges
The relation describes runtime classification, not guaranteed device support

benefits: One DOM-facing component contract across framework choices
costs: DOM lifecycle and browser constraints remain part of application correctness
Adapters add compatibility and release coordination cost

benefits: Reusable transitions for page stacks and transient UI
costs: Ordering, animation, and cleanup make state transitions nontrivial

benefits: Portable capability detection with native escape hatches
costs: Host signals and native bridges produce conditional behavior
